title: Compatibility of the exact-couple differential
statement:
Let $\square$ be a cartesian square with $f:X\to Y$, $g:Y'\to Y$, $f':X'\to Y'$, $g':X'\to X$, let $K\in\Dplus(X_{\Et})$ have torsion cohomology with $\mathcal H^q(K)=0$ for $q<a$, and let $A_q=g^{-1}Rf_*\tau_{\leq q}K$, $G_q=g^{-1}Rf_*\mathcal H^q(K)[-q]$, $B_q=Rf'_*g'^{-1}\tau_{\leq q}K$, $H_q=Rf'_*g'^{-1}\mathcal H^q(K)[-q]$, the two exchanged truncation triangles $A_{q-1}\xrightarrow{i_q}A_q\xrightarrow{j_q}G_q\xrightarrow{k_q}A_{q-1}[1]$, $B_{q-1}\xrightarrow{i'_q}B_q\xrightarrow{j'_q}H_q\xrightarrow{k'_q}B_{q-1}[1]$ and the exchange maps $e_q=\Ex_{\square,\tau_{\leq q}K}$, $\bar e_q=\Ex_{\square,\mathcal H^q(K)[-q]}$ between them be as in [def-weil-pbc-truncation-exact-couples] [def-weil-pbc-derived-exchange]. Use the standard cohomological shift convention $(M[1])^r=M^{r+1}$, $d_{M[1]}=-d_M$, so that $\mathcal H^{n}(M[1])=\mathcal H^{n+1}(M)$, and let the connecting maps $k_q$, $k'_q$ be the images of the connecting map of $\tau_{\leq q-1}K\to\tau_{\leq q}K\to\mathcal H^q(K)[-q]\to$ followed by the shift-commutation isomorphisms of $g^{-1}Rf_*$ and $Rf'_*g'^{-1}$ (the identity for the inverse images [def-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image]; for $Ru_*$ [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] the comparison of the K-injective resolutions $K[1]\to I(K[1])$ and $K[1]\to I(K)[1]$ [def-weil-pbc-kinjective-resolutions]). Index the two couples as in [def-sp-exact-couple]: $D_A^{p,q}=\mathcal H^{p+q}(A_q)$, $E_A^{p,q}=\mathcal H^{p+q}(G_q)$, $\alpha=\mathcal H(i_{q+1})$, $g=\mathcal H(j_q)$, $f=\mathcal H(k_q)$, and likewise $D_B,E_B$. Then:

(1) both are exact couples, and $t_D=\mathcal H^{p+q}(e_q)$, $t_E=\mathcal H^{p+q}(\bar e_q)$ form a morphism of exact couples; in particular they commute with the connecting maps: $\mathcal H^{p+q+1}(e_{q-1})\circ\mathcal H^{p+q}(k_q)=\mathcal H^{p+q}(k'_q)\circ\mathcal H^{p+q}(\bar e_q)$;

(2) the induced maps $E_{A,r}\to E_{B,r}$ ($r\geq2$) of the spectral sequences of the two couples commute with every differential $d_r$;

(3) the $E_2$ map in bidegree $(p,q)$, read through the identifications $\mathcal H^{p+q}(G_q)\cong g^{-1}R^pf_*\mathcal H^q(K)$ and $\mathcal H^{p+q}(H_q)\cong R^pf'_*g'^{-1}\mathcal H^q(K)$ given by the same shift-commutation isomorphisms and $\mathcal H^{p+q}(N[-q])=\mathcal H^p(N)$, is the degree-$p$ exchange map of the torsion sheaf $F=\mathcal H^q(K)$,

$$
 \mathcal H^p(\Ex_{\square,F}):\ g^{-1}R^pf_*\mathcal H^q(K)\longrightarrow
 R^pf'_*g'^{-1}\mathcal H^q(K).
$$

proof.text: Apply AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.truncation_exchange_couple_morphism to sq and K. Its first conjunct supplies exact couples P and Q and all D/E equalities and heterogeneous structure-map equalities. Its remaining conjuncts give the alpha, g and f exchange squares and the precise E2 comparison formula. The torsion and lower-bound hypotheses are not needed for these functoriality assertions.

Transport tD and tE by eqToHom along the supplied D/E equalities. Apply Mathlib CategoryTheory.conj_eqToHom_iff_heq pointwise; dcongr_heq evaluates the given heterogeneous family equalities at p and q, with the codomain type equalities obtained by congrArg and congrArg₂. For alpha and f, cancellation reduces the CoupleMorphism equations to the given alpha and f squares. For g, first cancel the equality isomorphism from bidegree (p+0,q-0) to (p,q), and use comp_eqToHom_heq_iff to remove the transport in initialG. The same pointwise Mathlib transport gives the initialG equation, which reduces to the supplied g square. This constructs a CoupleMorphism P Q with the required transported initial E map. No private transport helper is restated.

Apply derivedCoupleFunctoriality to this CoupleMorphism and take its first conjunct. The resulting family M n gives t n p q = (M n).tE p q. Its zero-page equality is exactly the required conjugated tE formula, its differential equation reversed is the displayed differential square, and its successor kernel/projection equation is exactly the required compatibility. Combine these with the exact couples, structure-map identifications, the original three exchange squares, and the original E2 formula from the first step.

split_report.summary: Checked against Stacks 0DDE (etale-cohomology.tex line 18708, 'some details omitted', via Cartan-Eilenberg spectral sequences) and Stacks Homology 011Q-011S (exact couples, derived couple), and against the blueprint nodes def-weil-pbc-truncation-exact-couples, lem-sp-couple-morphism, def-sp-exact-couple, def-sp-truncation-couple. The imported one-paragraph proof asserted that the exchange maps commute with the connecting maps 'by naturality'; naturality gives only two of the three squares, the third (with the connecting map k_q) needs the compatibility of Ex with the shift isomorphisms of g^{-1}Rf_* and Rf'_*g'^{-1}, which no node stated: new node lem-weil-pbc-derived-exchange-triangulated (unsplit). The same compatibility is needed for the E_2 identification H^{p+q}(Ex_{F[-q]}) = H^p(Ex_F). The statement was made precise (objects, indexing as in def-sp-exact-couple, shift convention, which identifications read the E_2 map), without changing its content. Proof now five steps: exactness of both couples (lem-sp-truncation-couple-exact plus exactness of g^{-1}, g'^{-1}), the morphism of triangles (new node), the morphism of exact couples (elementary), all pages and differentials (lem-sp-couple-morphism, with the derivation written out from Stacks 011R), and the E_2 map. def-weil-pbc-truncation-exact-couples is a real dependency (it defines the objects A_q, G_q, B_q, H_q, the triangles and the maps e_q, bar e_q); what it gives as 'first graded component' names only source and target, the identification with H^p(Ex_F) is Step 5 here. lem-sp-couple-morphism (unit sk-prop-av-pqf-finite) is used as a generic tool lemma, as the blueprint cites it. Mathlib: no exact couples; spectral sequences only from spectral objects.
